`rshd`: the remote shell's daemon.

## Synopsis

<strong>rshd</strong>

## Description

<strong>rshd</strong> takes <strong>rsh</strong>(1)'s connections on TCP port 514, and answers rsh's search for hosts on UDP port 514 with its host's name (<strong>hostname</strong>(1)). It's a service: <strong>rc rshd start</strong> runs it, and <strong>rc rshd enable</strong> starts it at boot; it's off until then.

Each connection gets a session of its own (rshd runs itself with <strong>-s</strong>, the connection as its input, as inetd ran BSD's rshd). A login runs <strong>sh</strong> on a pty as big as rsh's terminal: what rsh sends is typed into it, so the pty does the terminal's work (echo, line editing, ^C), and what it shows goes back. A command runs with <strong>sh -c</strong>, on pipes: its input from rsh, its output and errors back apart, then how it ended. When rsh goes, a login's line hangs up (SIGHUP to its shell), and a command's input ends.

## Files

<strong>/etc/rc.d/rshd</strong>
: Its service.

## Notes

No passwords and no encryption: anyone whose network card reaches this computer's gets a shell on it, as with Berkeley's rshd before <strong>.rhosts</strong> files. Leave it off where that matters.

## See also

<strong>rsh</strong>(1), <strong>rcp</strong>(1), <strong>rc</strong>(1)
